[Benzinga news, 2026-10-29T12:28:55Z, by Kaustubh Bagalkote] Hyatt Bets on Luxury, Wins Big and Raises 2026 Growth Outlook
Hyatt (NYSE: H) stock rose premarket after beating Q3 earnings with $1.27 EPS and raising its full-year 2026 RevPAR growth forecast.
Hyatt Hotels Corporation (NYSE: H ) stock rose in Thursday’s premarket trading after the hotel operator reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its full-year revenue per available room growth forecast, supported by strong U.S. travel demand and higher management fees . Beats Earnings Estimates Hyatt reported adjusted earnings of $1.27 per share, beating analysts’ consensus estimate of 77 cents. The company reported an adjusted loss of 30 cents per share a year earlier . Revenue declined 2.41% year over year to $1.743 billion from $1.786 billion, narrowly missing Wall Street’s estimate of $1.747 billion, according to Benzinga Pro . Net income attributable to Hyatt reached $58 million, or 60 cents per diluted share. Adjusted net income totaled $122 million. Adjusted EBITDA increased 6.2% year over year to $295 million, or 19% after adjusting for assets sold in 2025. Gross fees climbed 15.2% to $327 million, driven by strong hotel performance and expansion. U.S. Travel Demand Drives Growth Comparable system-wide hotel revenue per available room (RevPAR) rose 7.2% year over year, led by luxury properties and strong leisure and group travel demand. U.S. RevPAR increased 8.2%, benefiting partly from the FIFA World Cup and the timing of Jewish holidays. However, comparable all-inclusive resort net package RevPAR declined 2.5%, primarily due to weaker demand in parts of Mexico. Base management fees increased 10%, while incentive management fees jumped 21.9%. Franchise and other fees rose 16.8%. Hyatt opened 3,808 rooms during the quarter. Its development pipeline expanded 12.1% to approximately 158,000 rooms. Net rooms growth reached 3.8% over the trailing 12 months. Meanwhile, World of Hyatt membership grew 19% to approximately 72 million. See More: Top Value Stocks Hyatt Raises 2026 Growth Forecast Hyatt expects full-year comparable system-wide hotel RevPAR growth of 5% to 5.5%, reflecting stronger third-quarter performance . The company forecasts net rooms growth of approximately 6% and net income of $240 million to $310 million. Hyatt projects adjusted EBITDA of $1.17 billion to $1.20 billion, representing growth of 14% to 17% on an adjusted comparison basis. Gross fees are expected to reach $1.32 billion to $1.335 billion. Adjusted free cash flow is projected at $580 million to $630 million. Balance Sheet and Shareholder Returns As of Sept. 30, Hyatt reported total debt of $4.4 billion and liquidity of $1.8 billion, including $495 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. Available borrowing capacity totaled $1.347 billion. Hyatt repurchased $147 million in shares during the quarter, bringing year-to-date shareholder returns to $336 million. Approximately $1.4 billion remained under its repurchase authorization. The company also raised its full-year shareholder returns forecast to $375 million to $425 million through dividends and repurchases. Hyatt declared a quarterly dividend of 15 cents per share, payable Dec. 7 to shareholders of record as of Nov. 23. H Price Action: Hyatt Hotels shares were up 2.81% at $178.22 during premarket trading on Thursday, according to Benzinga Pro data .
